title: Trung tâm dữ liệu tại vùng thiếu nước · Causes / Problems / Solutions
prompt: Some governments are considering limiting water-intensive data centres in drought-prone regions. What difficulties could this policy create, and how could they be addressed?

source.detail: Bài luyện mở rộng biên soạn riêng cho năm 2026. Tham khảo các nhóm chủ đề trong forecast công khai; tình huống, bài mẫu và phân tích được viết mới.
source.disclaimer: Không xác nhận đề này đã xuất hiện hoặc sẽ xuất hiện trong kỳ thi. Các chủ đề ngách được bổ sung để mở rộng phạm vi luyện tập; không gán xác suất ra thi.

keywords: Trung tâm dữ liệu tại vùng thiếu nước Hệ làm mát có thể tranh nước với hộ dân, nông nghiệp vào mùa khô, khi thêm người dùng công nghiệp khiến nguồn hạn chế càng khó quản. Vấn đề phù hợp là áp lực tăng thêm lên hệ nước cụ thể, không phải giả định mọi đầu tư số đều thân thiện môi trường.
instructions: Give reasons for your answer and include any relevant examples from your own knowledge or experience. Write at least 250 words.
paragraphs: Governments considering limiting water-intensive data centres in drought-prone regions must address its practical difficulties rather than assuming that the expected benefit guarantees successful implementation. The central implementation difficulty is that location restrictions may discourage investment and simply shift facilities elsewhere, especially when local officials cannot distinguish different cooling methods and their actual consumption. Addressing that difficulty requires attention to the specific circumstances of affected users rather than a blanket promise of improvement.

Location restrictions may discourage investment and simply shift facilities elsewhere, especially when local officials cannot distinguish different cooling methods and their actual consumption. This difficulty becomes more serious when permits are decided using headline capacity figures rather than local seasonal water availability and independently checked plans for dealing with prolonged drought. A blanket ban could send a project to a neighbouring region with equally scarce water, reducing local investment without solving the wider pressure on shared supplies.

Approval should require transparent water budgets, drought operating conditions and comparison of feasible cooling options, with essential domestic supply receiving clear priority. A verified water budget makes competing demands visible before construction, while drought conditions require operators to reduce consumption rather than expecting households to absorb every shortage. A proposed centre could obtain approval only with tested low-water cooling and an enforceable drought plan that preserves essential domestic supplies during extended dry periods. Neighbouring authorities should compare proposed demand within the same catchment, so refusing one permit does not simply transfer the project beyond an administrative boundary while leaving shared water pressure unchanged.
Data-centre permits should reflect seasonal water pressures and enforceable drought plans, with household needs protected before additional industrial demand is approved.
